item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, but slightly positive. In 2024 Kishida did push several policies that could improve ordinary people’s future life chances in durable ways, especially for children, women, and poorer regions. But the inherited baseline was weak and the macro constraints were severe: real wages and household purchasing power were still under pressure, and some equality-protecting institutions remained incomplete.

**Positive**
- [Policies supporting children and child-rearing](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/childsupport.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | The child-support package is designed as a universal, income-independent entitlement with reduced childbirth and higher-education burdens, so it is the clearest evidence that Kishida tried to improve the next generation’s life chances through a durable social institution. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- [Video Message from Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio on International Women's Day](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/08message2.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 8, 2024 | Kishida tied women’s empowerment to wage parity, executive appointments, work-family balance, and anti-violence protections, which is direct evidence of widening equal opportunity rather than just improving aggregate welfare. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | He backed broad subsidies for school lunches, childcare, care services, public transport, SMEs, and low-income households, which is a concrete attempt to cushion ordinary people against price shocks and preserve their life chances. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | Kishida linked wage growth, child support, women’s participation, regional revitalization, and fiscal reform into a longer-run policy program, which suggests an attempt to move beyond short-term relief toward better life chances. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- [Prime Minister Kishida’s statements on the former Eugenics Protection Law ruling](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 3, 2024 | Kishida apologized, promised compensation, and accepted state responsibility for forced sterilizations, which is direct redress for a grave dignity violation affecting marginalized people. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- [Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 29, 2024 | Kishida endorsed medium- to long-term projections, spending reform, and EBPM/“wise spending,” which matters for life chances because it makes social investment and redistribution more durable than ad hoc handouts. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.9`

**Negative / limiting**
- [Japan’s Kishida championed “new capitalism” but was undone by yen](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen) | Reuters | August 14, 2024 | Reuters said wage gains were real but were overwhelmed by the weak yen, high prices, and scandals, so the lived improvement in ordinary people’s purchasing power remained incomplete. | QIDs: `6B.10`
- [Japan’s real wages fall in March, marking 2 years of decline](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-indicators/japan-real-wages-fall-in-march-marking-2-years-of-decline-3430367) | Reuters | May 8, 2024 | Real wages were still falling, which is direct evidence against a claim that Kishida had already left ordinary households with materially better life chances by mid-2024. | QIDs: `6B.10`
- [Japan warns of weak yen impact on households in government white paper](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-warns-of-weak-yen-impact-on-households-in-government-white-paper-3551065) | Reuters | August 1, 2024 | The government itself warned that the weak yen was hurting household sentiment and purchasing power, showing that the baseline constraint on life chances remained severe. | QIDs: `6B.10`
- [World Report 2024: Japan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/japan) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | HRW said Japan still lacked a national human rights institution and that criminal justice remained abusive, which undercuts the claim that Kishida left behind strong rights-protecting institutions. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- [Japan: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Freedom House still flagged gender and ethnic discrimination, exclusion of some ethnic Koreans from elections, and persistent equality gaps for LGBT people and asylum seekers, so opportunity gains were real but incomplete. | QIDs: `6B.10`, `6B.8`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence of intended institutional change, but not direct 2024 outcome data proving that mobility, earnings, education, or health trajectories had already improved for ordinary people by year-end.
- The best-supported positive case is policy design and entitlement expansion; the best-supported negative case is that inflation, yen weakness, and structural rights deficits still limited realized gains.
